name: vanilla crinkle cookies
instructions:
Nicole Rucker's crinkle-style cookie WITHOUT the chocolate — lightly crisp, crackly exterior and squidgy cakelike interior, with rainbow sprinkles. The coconut oil is one of the major secrets: DO NOT SKIP IT — it adds texture after the cookies have completely cooled, and a subtle flavor of grocery-store cake.

MAKES 12 COOKIES.

=== INGREDIENTS ===

- 2 1/3 cups (290g) unbleached all-purpose flour
- 1 tsp (4g) baking powder
- 1/2 cup (100g) granulated sugar, + more for rolling the cookies
- 1/3 cup (38g) sifted confectioners' sugar, + more for rolling the cookies
- 1/2 tsp (1.5g) Diamond Crystal kosher salt
- 7 oz (198g) COLD unsalted butter, cubed
- 1 tbsp (14g) unrefined extra-virgin coconut oil
- 2 large eggs (100g)
- 2 tsp (10g) vanilla extract
- 1/4 cup (50g) rainbow sprinkles

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. In a stand mixer with the paddle, MIX the flour, baking powder, sugars, and salt — disperses the powder and breaks up sugar lumps.
2. ADD the cold butter and coconut oil; mix on LOW until the mixture resembles RUSTIC SAND, about 4 minutes.
3. ADD the eggs, vanilla, and sprinkles. Mix on low until the eggs are completely incorporated and you have a thick dough.
4. PREHEAT the oven to 375°F (190°C). Line two half sheet pans with parchment.
5. PORTION the dough into 12 balls with a spoon. Roll them in GRANULATED sugar, then in CONFECTIONERS' sugar. Transfer to a plate or quarter sheet pan and FREEZE 30 MINUTES. Once chilled, roll each ball in confectioners' sugar ONCE MORE.
6. Place six well-spaced balls per sheet. BAKE 10 minutes on the two center racks, ROTATE the pans, bake another 5-6 minutes — until puffy and set at the edges. Centers will look cooked but a light touch on top gives a subtle puffy, squishy give.
7. EAT THEM FRESH, just after cooling. Store uneaten cookies sealed in the fridge; for best results, warm 15 seconds in the microwave to refresh before eating.
notes:
=== WHY I LIKE IT ===

They taste like PLAYDOUGH somehow. That's it — that's the note.

=== AUTHOR'S SECRETS (RUCKER'S) ===

- THE COCONUT OIL — do not skip it: it adds texture after the cookies have completely cooled, plus the subtle grocery-store-cake flavor.
- The double sugar roll (granulated, then confectioners', then confectioners' AGAIN after the freeze) is what builds the crackly crinkle exterior.
- Crinkle architecture without chocolate: lightly crisp crackly exterior, squidgy cakelike interior.
